studies.Population: Men in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study without prior cancer who completed the adolescent diet questionnaire
studies.Reference: Adolescent Plant Product Intake in Relation to Later Prostate Cancer Risk and Mortality in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study.
studies.Authors: Lan T, Park Y, Colditz GA, Liu J, Wang M, Wu K, Giovannucci E, Sutcliffe S
studies.Timing: Adolescent intake at ages 12–13 years; prostate cancer follow-up through 31 December 2011
studies.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest quintile of adolescent vegetable protein intake (Q5 versus Q1), advanced prostate cancer
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: The supplementary risk factor questionnaire included a 37-item FFQ that assessed participants’ diet at ages 12–13 y.

sample_size.excerpt: The final analytic cohort included 150,671 men.
sample_size.location: Methods, Study population and design, final paragraph

cases.excerpt: Cox proportional hazards regression was used to calculate HRs and 95% CIs of nonadvanced (n = 14,238) and advanced (n = 2,170) PCa incidence and PCa mortality (n = 760) during 1,729,896 person-years of follow-up.

effect_size.location: Table 2, Vegetable protein, % of kcal, Advanced PCa row

confidence_interval.location: Table 2, Vegetable protein, % of kcal, Advanced PCa row

p_value.excerpt: Positive trends were also observed for greater intakes of fruit juice ( P -trend = 0.002), total fruit ( P -trend = 0.014), and dark bread ( P -trend = 0.035) with nonadvanced PCa risk and for greater intakes of legumes ( P -trend < 0.001), fiber ( P -trend = 0.001), and vegetable protein ( P -trend = 0.013–0.040) with advanced PCa risk or PCa mortality.
